intended_object: For a closed (degree-0, differential-commuting) morphism f : M → N of right curved DG modules over a curved DG algebra (A, d, w), this is the cone sequence N → Cone(f) → M[1], made of the canonical inclusion and projection, viewed as a short complex. Inferred from the docstring, the module doc (Positselski §7.6) and its later use as a graded-split conflation.
explanation: The body is `ShortComplex.mk (coneInclusion f) (coneProjection f) _`. Here `coneInclusion` is the closed map `LinearMap.inr : N → M × N`. It respects the cone grading `M^{p+1} × N^p` and the cone differential. `coneProjection` is the closed map `LinearMap.fst : M × N → M[1]`. Their composite is zero, which is the required proof. This is exactly the standard cone sequence N → Cone(f) → M[1], and the rest of the file shows it splits as graded modules, as the theory expects (Positselski). The setting is the library's category of curved DG right modules, so no extra hypotheses are imposed beyond those the notion needs. Mathlib has mapping-cone triangles only for ordinary cochain complexes (`CochainComplex.mappingCone`), not for curved DG modules, so there is no direct Mathlib counterpart and the definition is not too narrow.
